psychology.en: Firstly, the psychology of speaking to someone and feeling judged – we think is a key factor.
psychology.zh: 首先，和人说话并觉得自己被评判的心理——我们认为这是一个关键因素。

psychology.en: And finally, psychology makes us vulnerable to a post-truth world.
psychology.zh: 最后，心理学让我们在后真相世界中变得脆弱。

psychology.en: Modern psychology has borrowed and adapted these ideas into what we now call hedonic and eudaimonic happiness.
psychology.zh: 现代心理学借鉴并调整了这些理念，演变成了我们现在所说的享乐型幸福和实现型幸福。

psychology.en: Now, although the debate continues, Milgram's experiment is one of the most cited in the history of social psychology.
psychology.zh: 尽管争论至今仍未平息，但米尔格拉姆实验仍是社会心理学史上被引用次数最多的研究之一。

psychology.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode, the first part of our three-part mini-series on The Dark Side of Psychology.
psychology.zh: 好了，今天的节目就到这里，这是我们三集迷你系列《心理学的阴暗面》的第一部分。

psychological.en: And finally, coping strategies are psychological ways of managing your emotions in challenging situations.
psychological.zh: 最后，应对策略是在具有挑战性的情况下管理情绪的心理方式。

psychological.en: And there was the physical and psychological distance from the person being harmed.
psychological.zh: 此外，还有与受害者之间物理上和心理上的距离感。

psychological.en: Modern ethical guidelines for psychological experiments would see it as far too harmful.
psychological.zh: 按照现代心理学实验的伦理准则，这场实验的危害性实在太大了。

psychological.en: Instead, they needed to wage guerrilla warfare—hit-and-run attacks, sabotage and psychological pressure.
psychological.zh: 相反，他们需要进行游击战——游击袭击、破坏和心理压力。

psychological.en: So I want to explore confidence from a slightly more psychological perspective.
psychological.zh: 因此，我想从一个稍微偏向心理学的视角来探讨自信。
